# Spec — Isolate Project module validation in per-file child processes
<!-- Generated by /skill:sdd-spec on 2026-08-08. Source: finalized grill isolate-validate-project-project-module-executio-20260808-16daa1f9, originating from issue #27. Status: approved -->
<!-- SDD-Tracking: issue=chichex/waica#27; grill=isolate-validate-project-project-module-executio-20260808-16daa1f9 -->

## Context

`validateProject` currently calls `loadProjectComponents` inside its parent-process work (`packages/mcp/src/validation.ts:724-743`), while the loader installs process-wide module hooks and imports every direct Project entry inside the long-lived MCP (`packages/mcp/src/project-component-loader.ts:49,149,335-366`). Global guards in `packages/mcp/src/stdio.ts:22-33` keep some late Project-code failures alive but also catch genuine server defects; they cannot contain `process.exit()`, infinite loops, native crashes, or ESM cache retention. Since issue #23, the parent additionally needs Project-owned `onUpdate` and `updateAfter` facts for scheduling validation (`packages/mcp/src/validation.ts:432-479`), so moving execution must preserve that behavior without sending live classes across IPC. ADR-0001 fixes project-first package resolution, ADR-0004 fixes scheduling semantics, and ADR-0007 fixes the per-entry process boundary chosen by the source grill.

## Expected behavior

- **CA-1 (HIGH) — Healthy validation parity.** Before implementation changes, capture a golden result from the existing side-effect-free Project-owned loader/reference/scheduling fixtures. After isolation, the same Project trees produce a deep-equal complete `validateProject` result: ordered findings with identical code, severity, file, ref and message; summary; `ok`; notes; provenance; and warnings. Project-owned typed refs still honor `options` precedence and string defaults, and inherited `onUpdate`/`updateAfter` facts still produce the issue #23 scheduling findings with the same attribution. The intentionally changed cache/side-effect fixtures are excluded from this parity golden and covered by CA-6.

- **CA-2 (HIGH) — One deterministic OS process per direct entry.** Every direct `.ts` file under `src/components`, then `src/roles`, then `src/states`, with filenames sorted inside each directory, executes in a distinct OS child whose PID differs from the MCP parent and from every other entry child. A single validation has at most one entry child active at a time. A second validation uses fresh PIDs; direct entries do not share globals or ESM cache. The child inherits the MCP host working directory rather than changing to the Project root, and no Project-owned module executes in the MCP parent.

- **CA-3 (HIGH) — File-local hard-failure isolation and existing finding codes.** A syntax error, module-scope throw, `process.exit(0)`, `process.exit(1)`, self-signal, exit before a terminal payload, or other file-attributable abnormal termination yields one file-attributed `component-load-failed` error. An asset import or strip-only TypeScript construct unsupported by Node remains a file-attributed informational `component-load-unsupported`. In every case, all later direct entries still execute and their metadata still participates in parent validation; no file failure becomes a tool failure or suppresses unrelated findings.

- **CA-4 (HIGH) — Five-second per-file timeout with proven termination.** The production per-entry deadline is exactly 5,000 ms from spawn through imports, top-level await, exported-class discovery, constructors, DTO projection and acknowledged terminal delivery. A child that exceeds it is force-terminated immediately, the parent waits for its `close`, and that file receives `component-load-failed`; validation then continues. There is no aggregate deadline and no public `timeout_ms` argument, so several hanging files are each attempted in deterministic order. Focused tests may inject a shorter deadline but must separately assert the production value.

- **CA-5 (HIGH) — Minimal, atomic validation DTO.** The private child protocol is versioned and bound to a per-child request token. Exactly one valid terminal message is accepted. For each exported component it may contain only component identity/source, typed-ref kind and `options` presence, relevant string defaults, inherited `onUpdate` presence, and `updateAfter` presence plus string values. Constructors, instances, methods and arbitrary runtime values never cross IPC. A wrong version/token, malformed row, duplicate terminal message, or any otherwise invalid payload rejects the entire entry atomically as `component-load-failed`; no partial component metadata from that file is retained. The parent adapts valid scheduling facts internally without changing the public engine scheduling API.

- **CA-6 (HIGH) — Resolution and deliberate re-execution semantics.** Relative imports keep the current direct/direct-plus-extension/directory-index behavior, and `@waica/engine`, `@waica/behaviors` and `@waica/archetype-platformer` still resolve project-first with the bundled fallback when the Project has no installation. A present but unloadable Project package is never silently replaced. Re-validating an unchanged entry executes its module scope again in a fresh process; editing it is visible on the next call; and a helper imported by two direct entries may execute once in each entry process. Within one call, observable entry side effects follow the deterministic CA-2 order.

- **CA-7 (HIGH) — Async completion, bounded diagnostics and parent restoration.** Top-level await completes before metadata is sent and remains subject to CA-4. Once the one terminal message is acknowledged, the child exits without waiting for floating timers, intervals, sockets or unawaited promises; delayed work cannot retain or later crash the MCP. The parent retains only the final 64 KiB of child stdout and 64 KiB of child stderr, never forwards child output to MCP stdout, discards successful output, and includes bounded tails only when useful for an abnormal failure. The process-wide `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException` guards added for in-process Project code and the parent loader's hook-context/module-cache machinery are removed; genuine MCP defects regain normal Node handling.

- **CA-8 (HIGH) — Independent concurrency, cancellation and shutdown cleanup.** Two `validate_project` calls for the same Project may overlap and have independent queues, tokens, timers, children and collected results. Cancelling one request through the MCP SDK `AbortSignal` force-terminates only its active direct child, starts no remaining entries, and propagates cancellation rather than returning a finding or tool-error result; the other call completes normally. Closing the MCP force-terminates and awaits every active direct validation child before close completes. Waica does not claim or attempt ownership of descendants deliberately spawned by trusted Project code, and cleanup is never reported as successful unless direct-child exit was observed.

- **CA-9 (HIGH) — Runner infrastructure and shipped artifact.** The child runner is available from both source/Vitest execution and the built MCP copied into the CLI. A missing, unlaunchable or handshake-incompatible runner that makes isolated execution unavailable fails `validate_project` once as the existing `tool-error`, rather than emitting one Project finding per entry. `pnpm test:dist` drives the packed CLI over real stdio, executes healthy Project TypeScript, observes an edit in a later validation, contains an entry that exits before replying, and proves the same MCP process still answers a subsequent tool call. No new runtime dependency, package version, Node floor or public MCP tool schema is introduced.

- **CA-10 (HIGH) — Own-property-safe transition action lookup.** State-machine transitions whose action is an inherited `Object.prototype` name such as `constructor`, `toString` or `valueOf` receive `input-action-unbound` unless `src/controls.json` declares that action as its own key with at least one binding. The state-transition path uses the same `isBoundAction` semantics already used by typed action refs.

- **CA-11 (LOW) — Accurate execution-boundary documentation.** `packages/mcp/README.md` and `.sdd/specs/waica-mcp.md` describe one five-second child per direct Project entry, parent-owned validation, repeated module execution, existing load-failure codes, and the facts that this is not a filesystem/network sandbox and does not own Project-spawned descendants. They no longer describe Project modules, global exception guards, shared hook context or ESM cache as living in the MCP process. Implemented issue #23/#24 specs remain historical records rather than being rewritten.

- **CA-12 (LOW) — Static-tool portability remains cross-platform.** Validation-child lifecycle uses Node's direct `ChildProcess` APIs without POSIX process groups, negative PIDs, shell commands or a Windows exclusion. Unit tests exercise lifecycle behavior through platform-neutral adapters, and package typecheck/build remain green. Actual execution on Windows is not asserted by the current macOS-only autonomy contract and remains an explicit verification gap rather than a claimed pass.

## Out of scope

- A capability or security sandbox for filesystem, network, environment variables, native modules, Workers or subprocess creation.
- Cleanup of descendants spawned by Project code, custom heap/memory quotas, or host-level denial-of-service protection.
- One process per validation, Worker-based isolation, process pools, parallel entry loading or an aggregate validation timeout.
- Executing Project-owned code from `list_components`, or serializing arbitrary params/defaults/runtime objects.
- Changes to the public engine scheduling API, finding-code set, `validate_project` input schema, Node floor, package versions or npm publishing.
- Run Session/browser/dev-server process ownership and the unrelated standalone `pnpm test:e2e` behavior.
- Adding Windows CI or a mandatory Windows human gate.
- Rewriting implemented issue #23 and #24 specs as if they were current design documents.

## Inferences

| # | Inference | Proposed choice | Reasonable alternative | Confidence | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bounded child diagnostics | Last 64 KiB per stdout/stderr stream; expose only for abnormal failures | 64 KiB combined or discard all output | high | confirmed |
| 2 | Forced termination policy | Force-terminate immediately and await `close`; no graceful period | `SIGTERM`, 250 ms grace, then force-kill | medium | confirmed |
| 3 | MCP cancellation result | Propagate SDK cancellation; emit no finding or tool-error result | Return a normal tool error | high | confirmed |
| 4 | IPC atomicity | Private versioned/token-bound protocol; one atomic terminal payload | Unversioned IPC with partial salvage | medium | confirmed |
| 5 | Child working directory | Inherit the MCP host cwd | Change cwd to the Project root | high | confirmed |
| 6 | Healthy-result parity | Deep-equal the complete deterministic result for side-effect-free fixtures | Compare finding sets only | high | confirmed |
| 7 | Timeout test strategy | Inject short test deadlines, assert production 5,000 ms, use real children | Wait a real five seconds in every timeout test | high | confirmed |
| 8 | Windows verification | Keep indirect portability signals at LOW; add no Windows gate | Require Windows CI or a human protocol | low | confirmed |
| 9 | Historical spec reconciliation | Update MCP README/waica-mcp spec; retain issue #23/#24 as historical | Rewrite every historical in-process reference | medium | confirmed |
| 10 | Dependencies | Use Node built-ins and the existing MCP SDK only | Add process/serialization dependencies | high | confirmed |

## Verifiability

**Mixed: CA-1 through CA-10 are HIGH; CA-11 and CA-12 are LOW.** The autonomy contract records `pnpm test` as a deterministic Vitest suite (805 tests in 86 files, about 3.6 seconds), making loader, protocol, process, cancellation and validation behavior directly observable with real local children and temporary Projects. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` cover cross-package and emitted-runner shape, while `pnpm test:dist` executes the packed CLI over real stdio and is the strongest available signal for CA-9. No browser interaction, external service or human judgment is required for CA-1 through CA-10.

CA-11 is LOW because grep/text assertions prove that documentation exists, not that readers interpret it correctly. CA-12 is LOW because the implementation can avoid POSIX-only mechanisms and exercise platform-neutral adapters, but `.sdd/project.md` records only a macOS host and no PR CI; actual Windows process behavior is not observed. There are no active generation policies for PR size, coverage, dependencies or commits, and the accepted built-in-only design introduces no policy conflict. The blast radius is one coherent MCP execution seam plus its packed smoke and documentation, so no spec split is required.

## Verification plan

The confirmed mechanism is **focused deterministic Vitest process integration plus the packed real-stdio smoke**, followed by the complete local ladder. Browser e2e is not added because it does not observe this process boundary more directly.

1. **Capture CA-1 baseline before code changes.** Run the existing focused loader/reference/scheduling fixtures and persist a handwritten/deep-equal golden of their complete `validateProject` outputs. Do not derive the expected value after changing the loader.
2. **TDD the process boundary.** Extend `packages/mcp/src/project-component-loader.test.ts` (and a focused child-runner test if separated) with real temporary Project entries that record PID, cwd, order, concurrency and repeated side effects. Use injectable launcher/deadline seams only to make timeout, malformed protocol and cleanup cases fast; the exercised production path still spawns real Node children.
3. **CA-1/CA-5 validation parity.** Run `pnpm exec vitest run packages/mcp/src/project-component-loader.test.ts packages/mcp/src/param-reference-validation.test.ts packages/mcp/src/validation.test.ts`; deep-equal refs, defaults, `options` precedence, inherited scheduling facts, class attribution and full result ordering.
4. **CA-3/CA-4 failure matrix.** Fixtures cover syntax, asset import, unsupported TS, throw, exit 0/1, self-signal, infinite loop, several timed-out files and healthy files after each failure. Assert 5,000 ms as the production constant, injected short deadlines in tests, one finding per failed file and observed direct-child exit before continuation.
5. **CA-6/CA-7 execution semantics.** Assert project-first, bundled fallback, extensionless/index imports, fresh execution per call, duplicate helper execution across entries, top-level await, prompt exit with a floating interval/socket/rejection, 64 KiB tails, clean success output and no parent hook contexts/global exception guards.
6. **CA-8 cancellation and shutdown.** Use the SDK's in-memory client/server transport and an `AbortController` in `packages/mcp/src/server.test.ts`; prove only the cancelled call stops, no later child starts, an overlapping call completes, and `server.close()` awaits all direct children. Lower-level tests force cleanup failure and assert it is not reported as success.
7. **CA-9 packaging.** Assert the emitted child entry in package/build tests, then extend `scripts/test-dist.mjs` so the packed CLI validates Project code, observes an edit, survives a file child exit and answers another real stdio request. Keep the existing packed Runtime Session regression leg unchanged.
8. **CA-10 regression.** Add state-transition cases for absent and explicitly bound `constructor`, `toString` and `valueOf`; assert exact `input-action-unbound` findings.
9. **CA-11/CA-12 indirect checks.** Grep README/waica-mcp for the process, timeout, trust and descendant limits and reject stale in-process wording. Assert the validation child path contains no detached process group, negative PID or shell cleanup mechanism. Report Windows as not executed.
10. **Focused command during red/green:** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/mcp/src/project-component-loader.test.ts packages/mcp/src/param-reference-validation.test.ts packages/mcp/src/validation.test.ts packages/mcp/src/server.test.ts packages/mcp/src/stdio.test.ts` (adjust only for a newly named focused child-runner test).
11. **Final required ladder:** `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm test:dist`. Report exact totals and the existing editor-chunk warning separately; do not claim standalone `pnpm test:e2e` or Windows was run.

## Risks and gaps

- Five seconds is a confirmed product deadline but not yet characterized on a slow Windows/Linux host. Tests must fail rather than silently extend it if a supported packed runner cannot start in time.
- One process per entry deliberately changes side-effect/cache semantics: every validation re-executes entry scope, and common dependencies can execute once per entry.
- Sequential timeouts have an accepted `N × 5s` worst case because complete per-file coverage wins over an aggregate deadline.
- This boundary protects the MCP process, not the host: trusted Project code can still modify files, use the network, spawn surviving descendants or exhaust host memory.
- Bounded stdout/stderr tails may contain local Project data; they appear only in local abnormal-failure diagnostics and never on MCP stdout.
- Cancellation requires threading the SDK handler's existing `extra.signal` through `execute`, `validateProject` and the loader without converting cancellation in the generic `errorResult` catch.
- Actual Windows execution remains LOW-verifiability and untested by the current contract; avoiding POSIX-only APIs is an indirect signal, not proof.
- `pnpm test:dist` includes the existing Chrome-backed Runtime Session leg even though this feature is static-process work; the contract requires compatible host Chrome for the full ladder.
- No CI runs on PRs, so all autonomous evidence is local and must be copied into the eventual PR.
- ADR-0001 was reconciled and ADR-0007 was approved during the source grill's domain-modeling close; implementation and docs must remain consistent with both.
